title: Stream redelivery policy and shedder protocol harmonization for cross-tenant queues
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Our Redis and Kafka worker fleets handle retries, poison messages, and shedding inconsistently across tenants. Symptoms: tenant A experienced burst-driven latency spikes because consumers accepted messages while downstream KV cache was hot-locked; tenant B lost visibility into redelivery attempts because we mixed exponential retry timers with lease-based requeues. This ticket consolidates a single redelivery policy (lease+delayed-requeue) and a common shedder protocol that propagates explicit backpressure signals from the serving runtime into ingress shards. Goals: 1) Replace ad-hoc retry timers with a lease-backed redelivery flow that records intent and attempt counts in a compact stream header. 2) Extend the shedder protocol to support immediate rejection, soft-defer (short delay), and lease-extension signals so upstream ingress can pause routing to specific shards. 3) Ensure idempotency headers and DLQ paths are standardized across Redis/Kafka consumers. 4) Add observability: per-tenant redelivery histogram, shed events, and a small tracing tag to follow message lifecycle across services. Trade-offs considered: - Aggressive lease durations increase visibility but add lease churn; we'll default to conservative 30s leases and expose config per deployment tier. - Synchronous shed propagation reduces throughput but prevents cascading queue pile-ups; we designed async control-plane hooks to avoid head-of-line blocking. Plan: 1) Spec (this ticket) -> design doc + sequence diagram (link below). 2) Prototype: add lease metadata to Redis stream XAdd and Kafka message headers, implement a small lease-keeper library used by both consumer shims. 3) Routing change: ingress shards read shedder decisions via a lightweight Redis pubsub topic and will stop dispatching to busy consumers for the bucketed key range. 4) Backfill: migration tool to annotate in-flight messages with lease metadata when possible. 5) Feature flags and canary rollout: start with Dedicated clusters, run for 1 week, then flip for hosted API. Links: design notes https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-redwood-lease-shedder, prototype PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621
